text:
sam: heads-up: since last deploy we're seeing sporadic 5-20% packet loss between east-west GPU inference pods in us-west2. SLO alerts spiking.

maria: timeline? did we upgrade anything in the cluster late last night?

sam: cilium daemonset rolled ~00:12UTC to 1.19.1 across west2-gpu pool. kube-proxy still on, but noticed datapath new fragmentation handling flagged in logs.

chen: confirming — I pushed the operator upgrade at 00:10 and rsync finished by 00:15. didn't change MTU configs explicitly.

leo: observed ICMP ping jitter and also MTU mismatch on vxlan devices on nodes with RDMA NICs.

anya: can you paste outputs? especially `ip -d link` and `ethtool -k` for one of the affected nodes.

sam: paste: 
```
# ip -d link show cilium_vxlan0
6: cilium_vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 8950 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    gso_max_size 65536 gso_max_segs 65535
```

sam: and on the RDMA NIC:
```
# ethtool -k mlx5_0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
lro: off
```

maria: MTU 8950 — we used to be 9000. Did the cilium config switch to vxlan with inner-header footprint change?

chen: yes, upstream changed default overlay for this kernel/hw profile; it adds ~50 bytes overhead for inner encapsulation unless `native-routing-cidr` is set. Some of our RDMA paths don't do fragmentation well.

leo: hypothesis: GSO/TSO on NIC + tunnel encapsulation causing packets > MTU to be mis-segmented -> blackhole when RDMA-enabled stack expects in-order large frames.

anya: quick mitigation: set GSO off on cilium tunnel device and lower MTU to 8800 to be safe. will that break perf?

sam: runbook test on staging: toggled `net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1` and disabled GSO on cilium_vxlan0 -> packet loss dropped to ~0.5% within 2min; throughput ~-4%.

chen: commands I ran on staging:
```
# sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1
# ethtool -K cilium_vxlan0 gso off gro off tso off
```

maria: okay - we should create a canary rollout: patch cilium DaemonSet with `tunnelMTU: 8800` and add a poststart hook to toggle GSO on affected nodes only; also open a rollback path.

leo: also need to check conntrack buckets - saw surge in conntrack entries after upgrade. might be related to new masquerade rules.

anya: I dumped conntrack and saw a lot of `ASSURED` TCP entries stuck in TIME_WAIT for flows using hostport: GPU service -> adding `--conntrack-max-per-core` might help.

sam: action items:
- chen: create cilium patch with explicit mtu and gso toggle (canary) - DONE/ETA 30m
- maria: throttle canary to 5% of GPU nodes and monitor pod-to-pod p99 latency + packet loss - ETA 10m
- leo: check RDMA drivers/firmware on canary nodes and collect `dmesg` - ETA 20m
- anya: prepare rollback and a kernel param list; update runbook with the `ethtool` commands - ETA 15m

ops-bot: deploy started for canary group gpu-node-pool-canary at 1823456920 by chen

sam: pinging perf dashboard, enabling extra pcap on canary nodes for 30m.

maria: if canary stable after 30m we can roll to 30% and then hourly.

leo: FYI hardware vendor reported a known issue with mlx5 offloads + vxlan+gso on 5.x kernels.

chen: logging patch to PR and will attach canary rollout plan. I'll also add a note to avoid auto-upgrading Cilium on RDMA pools until we have a validated profile.

anya: thanks all — documenting final mitigation in infra-runbook/gpu-networking.md and tagging for postmortem if not resolved.

sam: thanks — will update thread with metrics.
